title: How to Clean a Cast Iron Skillet

seo.title: How to Clean a Cast Iron Skillet
seo.meta_description: How to clean a cast iron skillet without damaging seasoning, when soap is fine, and what to do about rust.
seo.search_intent: Resolve the household question clearly and safely, with practical decision points and next steps.

excerpt: Cast iron is best cleaned by hand with warm water, mild soap if needed, immediate drying, and a very thin coat of oil when appropriate.
content_html:
A cast iron skillet does not need a complicated ritual. For everyday care, hand-wash it, remove stuck food without prolonged soaking, dry it completely, and use an extremely thin film of oil when the surface needs protection.

Let the pan cool enough to handle safely

Do not move a screaming-hot skillet straight into cold water. Once it is safe to handle, scrape away loose food with a pan scraper or spatula.

Warm water and a little soap are fine

Lodge says modern dish soap can be used on seasoned cast iron. Scrub with a brush, sponge, or nonaggressive pad and rinse. For stuck food, a pan scraper or a short simmer with a little water can loosen residue.

Do not soak it

Exposed iron can rust. Leaving the pan full of water in the sink, allowing it to air-dry for a long time, or putting it in the dishwasher can strip seasoning and encourage rust.

Dry immediately and thoroughly

Use a towel or lint-free cloth. A few minutes of gentle heat on the stovetop can remove residual moisture. There is no need to overheat an empty pan.

Use less oil than you think

Once dry, a nearly invisible coat of cooking oil can help protect the surface. Wipe off the excess. A sticky finish usually means too much oil was left behind.

Surface rust is repairable

Rust does not automatically ruin a skillet. Lodge recommends scrubbing away the rust, washing and drying the pan, then reseasoning if a significant amount of the protective layer was removed. Steel wool is better reserved for rust restoration than routine cleanup.

Enameled cast iron is different

If your pan is enameled, it does not need seasoning and may have different cleaning instructions. Identify the cooking surface before following advice meant for bare seasoned iron.

The dependable routine is wash, dry completely, and protect. Most cast iron trouble comes from prolonged moisture, not from a small amount of dish soap.

faq.question: Can you use soap on cast iron?
faq.answer: Yes. A small amount of mild dish soap is fine on seasoned cast iron.

faq.question: Can cast iron go in the dishwasher?
faq.answer: Seasoned cast iron should generally be hand-washed; a dishwasher can strip seasoning and promote rust.

faq.question: What if the pan rusts?
faq.answer: Scrub away rust, wash and dry completely, then reseason if the protective layer was substantially removed.
